title: Delinquency Thresholds for Farm Real Estate Loans — Default Interest Add-On, Default Trigger and Nonaccrual Days
content:
Three delinquency thresholds are set for every FarmLand product of Farm Real Estate Loans:

- **Default-interest add-on** — the percentage points added to the contract rate on principal while an installment is past due beyond the default trigger.
- **Default-interest trigger days** — the calendar days an installment may stay unpaid past its due date before default interest applies.
- **Nonaccrual days** — the calendar days past due before nonaccrual.

| Product | Default-interest add-on (percentage points) | Default-interest trigger (calendar days) | Nonaccrual (calendar days past due) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FarmLand Variable-Rate Mortgage | 3.0 | 60 | 90 |
| FarmLand 3-Year Adjustable Mortgage | 3.0 | 60 | 90 |
| FarmLand 5-Year Adjustable Mortgage | 3.0 | 60 | 90 |
| FarmLand 10-Year Adjustable Mortgage | 3.0 | 60 | 90 |
| FarmLand 15-Year Fixed Mortgage | 3.0 | 60 | 90 |
| FarmLand 25-Year Fixed Mortgage | 3.0 | 60 | 90 |

**Reading the thresholds.** The three figures are uniform across the product family: an add-on of 3.0 percentage points, a default-interest trigger of 60 calendar days and a nonaccrual threshold of 90 calendar days past due, so the product's default-interest trigger falls 30 calendar days before the nonaccrual threshold.
